questions.question: broadcast in Indian radio has strengthened grassroots democracy. a. Short news bulletins based on national issues b. Advertisements on the new schemes of government c. Community radio programmes allowing public to create content d. Radio dramas based on Indian epics
questions.solution_html:
• History of Radio Broadcasting in India - Early Experiments (1920s-1930): Amateur radio
  • clubs in Calcutta, Bombay and Madras (from 1925) - aired programmes for more than two
  • hours. The Indian Broadcasting Company (IBC) began regular transmission in 1927 raising
  • funds through licence fees and import duties. It closed operations in 1930 - Public
  • Broadcasting (1930-1936): The government created the Indian State Broadcasting Service
  • (ISBS) in 1930 and took over Bombay and Calcutta stations. The Indian Tariff (Wireless
  • Broadcasting) Amendment Act, 1932 (doubling import duty on receivers) and the Indian
  • Wireless Telegraphy Act, 1933 (licence mandatory for ownership) together strengthened the
  • System - All India Radio (1936 onwards): In 1935, BBC producer Lionel Fielden and
  • engineer H. L. Kirke were invited to modernise broadcasting. Within a year a central
  • broadcast station was opened at Delhi and Fielden renamed ISBS All India Radio (AIR). The
  • plan emphasised medium-wave for cities and short-wave for connecting them.
  • Post-Independence Developments: At the time of Independence, India had 11 stations and
  • 248,000 licence holders. A pilot project sought to establish at least one station in every
  • linguistic region. AIR was put under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.
  • The Role of Radio in India
  • Radio matters in India - human voice builds trust and intimacy- relevant across genres
  • news, education, drama and music. During the Green Revolution radio was a key channel for
  • agricultural guidance and social development.
questions.source_exam: Dynamics of Radio Jockeying, Anchoring and Interviewing
questions.final_answer: agricultural guidance and social development.

questions.question: Compare live, recorded and deferred-live formats in terms of listener participation, editorial control and broadcast risks.
questions.solution_html:

  • editing and sound design.

  • mistakes go straight to air. Live shows require quick thinking and composure, though they
